EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  JANUARY 24, 2022

A special meeting of the Equestrian Committee of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was
called to order by CHAIR HUFF at 7:06 P.M. via teleconference, pursuant to the
Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20.
Committee Members Present:  Huff, Ciarolla, Griggs, Harik, Shinn
Committee Members Absent:  Brtis, Harik, Martin, Nilsen Zigrang
City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager, Alexa Davis
  Community Services Supervisor, Rosa Pinuelas
  Maintenance Superintendent, Mike Goldsmith
APPROVAL OF MINUTES
No quorum established. Meeting Minutes for November 29, 2021 will be moved to the
February 2022 Agenda.
AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN /ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA
None.
STAFF ITEMS
A.  EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG

  No discussion ensued; no action taken.

MEMBER SILVANO JOINED THE MEETING AT 7:15 PM. QUORUM OBTAINED.

B.  WESTERN BARRELS IN ARENAS
Superintendent Goldsmith provided a verbal overview per written report.

Superintendent Goldsmith responded to MEMBER HARIK that the City did not usually
offer barrels at City arenas.

MEMBER GRIGGS asked if the City could buy a set with locked storage. Superintendent
Goldsmith responded that the Committee may consider logistics of temporary barrels but
permanent barrels cause concerns with wear and tear of Arenas.

Assistant City Manager explained that even with temporary barrels, the logistics of
accessing them would have to be determined since maintenance staff is often out in the
field.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
JANUARY 24, 2022
  1
 MEMBER CIAROLLA asked if barrels could be moved and if they needed to be set-up at
the same spot each day to help reduce wear and tear. Superintendent Goldsmith
responded that if permanent barrels were installed it would cause wear and tear and
unfortunately, even temporary barrels would be an issue. MEMBER CIAROLLA asked if
the Committee could coordinate people to move barrels and jumps on a regular basis.
Superintendent Goldsmith responded that barrels should be moved daily.

Superintendent Goldsmith responded to MEMBER HARIK that barrels get knocked over
easily and explained that jumps also need to be moved but not as frequently and
maintenance staff is able to move them weekly.

CHAIR HUFF asked if equestrians could call and schedule checking out barrels in
advance for access.

MEMBER CIAROLLA explained that barrels were available at Chandler and Ernie Howlett
arenas but never observed them being used often. She expressed that western riding is
becoming more popular again, but was not sure that many people would use it. She
stated she wants to be supportive of the activity and asked the Committee if there would
be interest in the community.

MEMBER GRIGGS asked how many people have approached the City to use barrels.
MEMBER SHINN responded she has heard from one interested person.

Superintendent Goldsmith explained that he understands Western is becoming more
common, but sees people with temporary barrels and explained that permanent barrels
require a heavy amount of maintenance work.

MEMBER SILVANO asked how many western trainers have a City business license and
to possibly explore through them to see if there is a larger interest in the community. It
was suggested to contact trainer, Sean Martin.

MEMBER ROBINSON JOINED THE MEETING AT 7:23 PM

MEMBER SHINN asked if a western rider wants to use barrels, if they can take them in
and out of the Arena themselves. MEMBER HARIK responded that it is unlikely they will
be taken out and agreed that there was a lot of wear and tear on Arena with barrels.

MEMBER CIAROLLA suggested tabling the item to the next meeting and ask those
interested to join to explain interest. COMMITTEE agreed to moving item to February.

Superintendent Goldsmith stated temporary barrels cost $130 per set in response to
CHAIR HUFF’s question. He further explained that a local trainer uses portable barrels.

Superintendent Goldsmith responded that permanent barrels are estimated at $800
because it has to be smooth edging and has added maintenance cost, in response to
MEMBER GRIGGS.
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
JANUARY 24, 2022
  2
 CHAIR HUFF directed that staff return in February with the item for temporary barrel
consideration and that the greater equestrian community be aware that the item is coming
before the Committee.

C.  HORSE TRAINER LIST (VERBAL REPORT)

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas reported that there were 22 licensed trainers in
2021; as of today, there is only one 2022 renewal with three in process. She explained
that reminders will be sent out but appreciated the Committee reminding those in the
community as well.

MEMBER HARIK asked if there were still issues with online business license application.
MEMBER SILVANO responded that the December notice goes out but when someone
tries to renew their application it takes them in that present year, rather than the new year
about to start. Staff will report to the Finance Department the ongoing concerns.

D.  PROPOSED CHANDLER PLAYGROUND SURVEY (VERBAL REPORT)

Assistant City Manager Davis reported that a survey was developed and approved by the
Park and Activities Commission. The survey will be available to the public in the coming
weeks.

COMMITTEE REPORTS

A.  TRAIL (VERBAL REPORT)

MEMBER GRIGGS asked how the trail going to Ernie Howlett is managed with new
owners and City easement. Supervisor Goldsmith stated that the City does maintain the
trail and will make contact with new owners. MEMBER GRIGGS responded that the trail
seemed to be having work done and her understanding was that there was an easement
established.

MEMBER ROBINSON reported that the work done on Dapplegray trail was a noted
improvement and expressed appreciation. Superintendent Goldsmith responded that it
was a private trail through the homes association and a new property owner in the
neighborhood who also owns the land that MEMBER GRIGGS previously mentioned,
completed the work.

B. MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

None.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
JANUARY 24, 2022
  3
 FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

A.  AMBASSADOR PROGRAM

This item will come back to the Committee with more details.

MEMBER HARIK asked about the status of the equestrian recognition approved last year.
Assistant City Manager Davis responded that the Pepper Tree Foundation had still not
received donations equal to the cost of the project and staff planned to return with an
update and suggested modifications to the project to accommodate a reduced budget.
MEMBER HARIK inquired about the amount raised so far and offered to assist with further
fundraising.

CHAIR HUFF suggested that Pepper Tree Foundation funds may be worth considering.

CHAIR HUFF announced that this was her last meeting as Chair as each year City
Council rotates roles. She continued that she has had the honor of serving on the
Committee now for two years and the next Council Member proposed is Member Schmitz.
The Committee thanked Chair Huff for her leadership.

CHAIR HUFF adjourned the Equestrian Committee meeting 7:40 P.M.

Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

__________________________  __________________________
Alexa Davis  Britt Huff, Chair
Assistant City Manager

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
JANUARY 24, 2022
